unmapped_findings: The Fe-30Mn-1.2C (0 wt.% Al) alloy is the Al-free reference material of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP screening; in the as-homogenized state it shows the best mechanical behavior of that alloy (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE), while aging reduces UTS and TE and embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and temperatures above 500 °C.

The alloy classifies as a single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel: for Al contents below 5 wt.% a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature and the TWIP effect (dislocation hardening followed by mechanical twinning) is the primary strain-hardening mechanism.

The paper presents a temperature-sensitive constitutive strain-hardening model for low-SFE fcc TWIP steels that is applicable in principle to SIMPLEX-type compositions such as this Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy, but no model run or experimental validation specific to this as-homogenized Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample is reported.
